notes: Account summary: AmberWave is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for inference powering their personalization and real-time recommendation stack. High throughput, predictable latency, and strict residency needs (NA) are driving dedicated + VPC requirement.
AE/Jordan Park: long relationship with infra team; procurement timeline aggressive (Q2). Prioritizing performance guarantees over lowest unit price.

SE/Maya: drove POC — used Llama-2-70B-q4 and a trimmed 30B reranker. POC config: 8 reserved A100-style GPUs, contiguous VPC network, custom KV cache sizing. Observed steady-state: ~110k tokens/sec aggregate at 8-gpu baseline for mixed short/long chat workload.

POC ask from customer: minimum guaranteed throughput of 200k tokens/sec aggregate (to cover peak holiday traffic) or defined credits; per-model concurrency caps to avoid noisy neighbors; clear burst policy (2x baseline for short windows) — AmberWave pushed for 2x for up to 5 minutes.
Redwood proposal discussed: tiered guarantee model:
- Nominal guarantee: 150k tokens/sec sustained (purchased reserved pool), measured over 30m windows.
- Burst allowance: up to 3x nominal for 3 minutes (autoscaled buffer), billing for burst above nominal at burst-rate premium; credits if burst requested but not served.
- Concurrency caps: per-model soft cap default 400 concurrent streams, option to raise to 800 for critical routes with additional reserve commitment.

Negotiation points captured on call 2026-02-16: AmberWave wants stronger minimum (200k) and longer burst (5 minutes). Redwood concerned about capacity fragmentation and cross-tenant risk if burst is unlimited.

SLA measurement: customer wants p95 token latency <= 120ms and p99 <= 300ms (in-region) for text-generation workloads. Redwood requested to specify measurement at ingress API (not network) and agreed to include network egress metrics in a separate appendix.
Credits/penalties: AmberWave asks for service credits scaling with minutes below thresholds over calendar month; Redwood countered with capped credits and remediation playbook before credit triggers.

Routing/fallback requirements: must support automatic fallback to smaller model family (30B) with transparent latency/cost reporting. Fallback should be policy-driven: latency SLO breach -> failover, capacity breach -> degrade to cheaper model rather than hard 429s.

Reserved GPU planning: AmberWave infra wants pinned instance types (NVIDIA A100 equivalent), ability to request maintenance windows, and a plan to expand reserved pool by 2x during holiday season. Redwood to produce capacity plan and lead time for additional reserved GPUs (target 14–21 days).
KV/prefix cache: requirement to preserve session-level KV across autoscale and during model fallback for personalization continuity. SE note: will need sticky routing and cache warmup strategy.
Operational hooks requested: trace IDs in responses, per-route token accounting, alert webhooks for utilization >90% sustained, and runbook for degraded performance.
Security/compliance: SSO + SCIM, SOC2 attestation required before contract signature, KMS integration for model artifacts, and 90-day audit log retention minimum.

Pricing ask: flat monthly reserved fee + committed tokens/sec guarantee; clear overage pricing for sustained usage above guarantee and separate burst pricing. AmberWave willing to commit to a 12–24 month reserve for a better rate.

Legal/Procurement: procurement wants explicit language for maintenance windows (max 4 hours/month), notification windows, and SLA credit calculation formula. Legal already shared a redline (see drive link).
